Definition: to be (causatively, make) zealous, i.e. (in a bad sense) jealous or envious
BiblicalUsage: Jealousy runs both ways in Scripture: Elijah says he has been very jealous for the LORD God of hosts, Israel provoked God to jealousy with strange gods, God says He will be jealous for His holy name. Rachel envied her sister because she bore Jacob no children.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe there are two jealousies, and they are not the same: God's jealousy guards what is His by right, and ours grasps what is not ours. The first is love, the second is theft, and I want mine to look like His.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
